reads.found: ZERO divergences from our TEI. Confirms Migne's own readings behind three [var:] fired in chunk 0020: Ex 16:25 (Sabbata hodie Domino, non invenietis illud in agro), Jac 4:13 (Hodie et crastino ibimus in civitatem), and the bare (Isich). at 0350D VERS. 15, which Migne sets WITHOUT the [n:]-style parentheses our other notes carry. reads.source: Gallica IIIF native crops plus 4x enlargements of three disputed words; archive.org PDF rendered at 100 dpi whole-page and 400 dpi crops, printed corners read 351 / 352
reads.found: THREE DIGITIZATION LOSSES -- the two printings AGREE and our TEI does not, so all three are TEI patches, not Migne's defects, and no [sic:] was fired: 0352A plate 'edebat' vs our 'edehat'; 0352D plate 'fornicantur' vs our 'tornicantur'; 0352D plate note '(I Cor. xi.)' vs our '(I Cor. XL.)'. Also observed: Gallica prints NO terminal stop after 'sanctorum vindicans injuriam' where our TEI supplies one (the archive appears to carry a stop; treated as a press variant and left alone). Confirms Migne's own '(Eccli. xix)' on the 3 Rg 1:33 quotation and '(Matth. viii)' on the Mt 9:8 allusion -- both misfired citations are HIS.

reads.source: Gallica IIIF native crops plus 4x enlargements; archive.org PDF at 100 dpi whole-page and 400 dpi crop, printed corners read 353 / 354
reads.found: ONE DIGITIZATION LOSS, confirmed on BOTH printings: 0354A the note reads '(Psal. xxxiii.)' -- Migne's citation of Ps 33:17 is CORRECT and our TEI's '(Psal. XXXVIII)' is the corruption. TEI patch filed; the English keeps the twin's form because verify-english content-checks [n:] against the Latin. ONE PRESS VARIANT: 0354C Gallica breaks 'tan' / 'git' across the line with NO hyphen (our TEI's 'tan git'), while the archive prints 'tan-' cleanly; one printing only, so no marker and no patch -- the English renders 'touches'. Nothing else diverges.

reads.source: Gallica IIIF native crops plus 4x enlargements of two disputed spots
reads.found: ZERO divergences from our TEI. Two things settled here that would otherwise read as findings: (1) 0359A the sentence 'non ut claudus, qui saltem cum infirmitate tenebat' BREAKS OFF on the plate itself, with no terminal stop and no completion before the next VERS. -- Migne's own truncation, not a digitization loss, so no [ed:]; (2) the numeral 3 in this fount prints with a flat top and reads as '5' at scan resolution -- 'Vers. 5. -- Omnis homo qui accesserit' at 0360A is Migne's Vers. 3, exactly as our TEI has it, and the same glyph accounts for 'Vers. 15' = 13 at 0350B and 'Vers. 25' = 23 at 0351C. Confirms Migne's own '(I Tim. ii.)' on the Titus 1:7 quotation at 0359C.
